samples.marker_line: OFX ETW-target variant: ransom encryption and Discord RAT; adds gates
OFX AMSI-target variant: ransom encryption and Discord RAT; adds gates
macOS phishing installer: saves password; adds staged execution traits

reverse_engineering.native_identification: Two 443392-byte unsigned x64 PE variants of an OFX-extension encryptor and Discord RAT. Resources claim Microsoft Corporation / Windows System Cache / syscache.exe; these are unverified claims, not Microsoft provenance. The specimens match the target mutations described by the existing checked-in OFX regression generator and differ from each other at only file offsets 0x17085 and 0x1728e. The generator and previous review were leads; instruction and data flow were independently inspected.
reverse_engineering.native_encryption: Main 0x140016d20 reaches 0x140003750, which generates a 32-byte session key and 12-byte nonce. 0x1400036c0 selects AES and ChainingModeGCM. 0x140003830 calls BCryptEncrypt at 0x1400038f1. File processing calls this worker at 0x140006676 and 0x1400067d0, then writes encrypted buffers through an indirect NT file wrapper. Successful processing sets FileDispositionInformation (class 13, one-byte true) on the original at 0x1400068a1. 0x140003920 imports an RSA public blob and encrypts the session key; 0x1400160a0 builds the payment-conditioned decryptor demand and key blob. Main writes notes and copies itself for reactivation. No authorized encryption workflow is supplied.
reverse_engineering.native_remote_control: 0x140014bb0 builds /channels/<id>/messages?limit=1 and requests message history. The main task loop reaches dispatcher 0x1400131f0. !exec appends received arguments to cmd.exe /c, calls the pipe-capturing child-process helper 0x140012340 and formats the output for the channel. !dl reads an operator-selected local file and calls multipart uploader 0x140010bb0. !screen calls GDI/PNG capture helper 0x14000e5a0, writes the returned buffer to a temporary PNG, uploads that same path at 0x1400146a6 and deletes it at 0x1400146c6. !up passes the supplied HTTPS URL and a generated temporary executable path to 0x140011e10; that helper checks the HTTP response, opens the supplied output path, and writes response bytes. Its success branch launches the same path with CreateProcessW at 0x140014332. Startup also constructs a host/encryption report. Downloaded final payload contents are not present.
reverse_engineering.native_persistence: 0x1400161f0 obtains its module path and an application-data destination. CopyFileW at 0x1400167db copies the image. The decoder at 0x140016880 reconstructs Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run; HKCU is opened at 0x14001693a, then RegSetValueExW at 0x140016a49 stores the copied path. This supports the existing self-copy/Run-key trait without depending on a chosen filename.
reverse_engineering.native_obfuscation: For string byte j, state=(seed-j*multiplier)&0xffffffff and plaintext=ciphertext^((state^(state>>15))&255). Decoder operands and stack initializers were read from each specimen, rather than treating trait names as plaintext. FNV-1a hashing and manual PE export lookup follow the name decoder.

native_security_patches.different-etw-target.exe: Loop 0x140017ca0 reconstructs AmsiScanBuffer; the resolved export is made writable and receives B8 57 00 07 80 C3 (mov eax,0x80070057;ret) at 0x140017daa. Loop 0x140017eb0 instead reconstructs EtwEventWritx. The stock ETW export is therefore not established; the ETW bypass trait correctly does not fire. The zero-return write instructions remain accurate neutral observations.
native_security_patches.different-amsi-target.exe: The first target is AmsiScanBuffex, so the AMSI bypass trait correctly does not fire. The second target is EtwEventWrite; after export resolution and VirtualProtect, 0x140017f3b writes 33 C0 C3 (xor eax,eax;ret). The invalid-argument write stub remains present as a neutral observation.

reverse_engineering.native_environment_gates: Startup tests the PEB BeingDebugged byte and debugger APIs. Existing uptime/CPU coverage corresponds to a 300000-ms threshold and at least two processors. Newly covered RAM and screen checks call GlobalMemoryStatusEx and GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN/SM_CYSCREEN), read the physical-memory result, and compare against 2 GiB and 1024x768. All three rejection branches target 0x1400180be, which returns from main. The new matcher binds the input structure to the physical-memory field, resolves each IAT operand, and checks equal branch destinations. This adds suspicious resource-gating coverage; low resources alone are not a hostile verdict.
reverse_engineering.shell_identification: A small macOS shell credential-phishing and clipboard-transfer installer specimen. Its SHA-256 exactly matches the checked-in hostile/validated-installer-clipboard.sh regression fixture. All endpoints use reserved .invalid names, so this does not establish live infrastructure or delivery. The malicious judgment concerns the program behavior visible in the bytes.
reverse_engineering.shell_execution_flow: Without set -e, it creates a temporary file, downloads a script to that variable path, invokes /bin/sh with the same path, and removes it. It then gets the current username, repeatedly displays an AppleScript hidden-answer dialog, verifies the captured value with dscl . -authonly, and only breaks on successful authentication. printf writes that same validated password to $HOME/.setup-secret. The HTTP form contains pbpaste output, scutil --get ComputerName and the first argument. It does not send the captured password in this visible HTTP request. It downloads a plist into the user LaunchAgents directory and invokes launchctl load on that path. The plist and first downloaded stage are unavailable from the reserved domain, so their contents, successful execution and autorun settings are not asserted. No privilege escalation is established.
reverse_engineering.judgment_basis: Both PE variants implement destructive extortion and operator-controlled access, outweighing any legitimate explanation for their low-level APIs. The shell validates and retains the actual local password in plaintext, combines that with clipboard transfer and downloaded LaunchAgent loading, and supplies no legitimate password-storage purpose. Standalone discovery on a machine would warrant MALICIOUS for all three. Their regression-fixture provenance is documented; actual deployment authorization and runtime success are unknown.

rule_changes.existing_detection_review: All existing findings retained. In particular, the missing AMSI/ETW traits correspond to altered target bytes, not a detection gap. The shell exfiltration trait describes clipboard transfer accompanying password capture and does not claim that this POST transmits the password. All new names and paths describe matcher-supported behavior; no sample-specific endpoint, filename, hash, or file offset gates a new rule.
rule_changes.consumers: Reviewed exact and ancestor references for new capabilities and sandbox suite membership. New source-only capabilities do not affect binary-only consumers; clipboard-read and host-name selectors gain accurate operations. Sample diffs show no unintended new composites. Full-corpus verification is the final make validate action.
rule_changes.limits: The PE resource rule recognizes the observed x64 compiler instruction shape with variable stack offsets, IAT operands, thresholds and branch displacements. It does not claim generic recovery of every resource gate. Native URL-fetched executable activation remains represented by HTTP, file-write, CreateProcess and RAT tasking observations; a separate fully call-bound native download/execute trait is not added because the generic facts do not carry that interprocedural path/buffer relationship. A broad conjunction would overstate the link. The shell download/execute gap is closed by an adjacent-command AST rule with equal variable names. No runtime-only behavior is introduced.

verification.existing_regression_checks: testdata/batch-5794-aedf-8b/check.py: 5 focused fixtures and 2 existing attack fixtures passed
verification.corpus_expectations: Existing hostile shell expectation now requires all five new neutral capabilities. Four benign variable-download fixtures require the positive chain and forbid mismatched-path, literal-dollar and opposite-branch chains.
verification.sample_execution: None: source inspection, facts, disassembly, arithmetic decoding and static control scans only.
